column2: His many-formed rays that go downward, of gentle lustre — by these he moves about here for the enjoyment of karma.
All the sense-organs of knowledge, the mind, the organs of action, the ego and the intellect, and the elements beginning with earth...
The unmanifest Self, the knower of the field, is spoken of as the one who stands in the field; he is the Lord of all beings, being and non-being, both existent and non-existent.
From the unmanifest arises the intellect, from it the ego; from the ego come ether and the rest, each with one more quality than the last.
Sound, touch, form, taste and smell are their qualities; whatever rests on anything dissolves into that very thing.
Sattva, rajas and tamas are declared his qualities; pervaded by rajas and tamas he is whirled like a wheel.
He who is without beginning yet has a beginning is indeed the Supreme Person; that which is grasped by the subtle body and senses is called the modification.
From whom come the gods, the Puranas, the sciences and Upanishads, the verses, sutras, commentaries, and whatever other speech there is...
By the path of the ancestors, the Vithi, and the space of Agastya, householders who keep the sacred fire and desire offspring go to heaven.
Those devoted to giving, with the eight qualities, the eighty-eight thousand sages who are householders...
...are the seed of return and establish dharma; those on the path of the Seven Sages go to the world of the gods.
An equal number of sages, free of all undertakings, through austerity, celibacy, renunciation of attachment, and intelligence...
...stay wherever they are until the dissolution at the call. Study of the Veda, sacrifices, celibacy, austerity, self-control,
faith, fasting and truthfulness are the causes of knowledge of the Self. By all the orders of life that Self is to be meditated upon in this way.
It is to be seen, to be reflected on, and to be heard by the twice-born. Those who know it thus and those who rely on the forest teaching...
...the twice-born who worship truth with supreme faith, in order attain the flame, the day, the bright half, and the northern course.
The path of the gods, the sun with lightning; then a person who is mind-born comes to them and leads them to the worlds of Brahma.
There is no return for them here. But those who win heaven by sacrifice, austerity and gifts...
...go by smoke, night, the dark half, the southern course, the world of the ancestors, the moon, sky, wind, water and earth.
In order they come to be here and go again. He who does not know these two paths of the Self...
...becomes a snake, a moth, an insect or a worm. Brahman is like a lamp in the heart; through meditation the soul becomes dead (to rebirth).
One whose wealth is rightly gained, who is devoted to knowledge of truth, fond of guests, performs the shraddha and speaks truth — even a householder is liberated.
From fire come water, from water earth, and then the subtle body; from the elements not yet quintuplicated, these quintuplicated ones arose.
Having meditated on the gross body, one should contemplate its dissolution in Brahman. The quintuplicated elements and their product are called Virat.
This gross body is imagined by knowledge of the Self. The wise know the waking state as awareness through the senses.
The one identified with it is Vishva; these three are non-agents. The unquintuplicated elements and their product are called the subtle body.
Joined with seventeen parts, it is named Hiranyagarbha; the subtle body of the Self is called the "linga".
Dream is born of impressions from waking, a cognition whose content is objects; the Self identified with it is Taijasa, without the world-spread.
The one cause of the two, the gross and subtle bodies, is the Self and knowledge with reflection; this is called superimposition.
It is neither being nor non-being nor both; it is not with parts, nor without parts; neither different nor not different, yet different.
Different and non-different, indescribable, it causes bondage and samsara. The One is Brahman, attained by knowledge, not by works.
The withdrawal of all the senses into their cause is the state of the intellect, deep sleep; the one identified with both is...
Prajna. The Self and these three are held to be "m", the Pranava: "a", "u", and "m" are this very thing.
I am the witness, mere consciousness, of waking, dream and the rest; ignorance and its effect, the bonds of samsara and so on, are not mine.
Eternal, pure, free from bondage, truth, bliss, without a second — I am Brahman; I am the supreme light, liberated. Om.
I am Brahman, supreme knowledge; samadhi destroys bondage. Brahman is lasting bliss, truth, knowledge, infinity.
This Self is Supreme Brahman, "That is Brahman", "You are That" — the soul, instructed by the teacher, is "I am Brahman", even outwardly.
That Person in the sun, I am he, the undivided. Om. The knower of Brahman is freed from this worthless samsara and becomes Brahman.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of mind and intellect; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of thought and ego.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of prana and apana; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of vyana and udana.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of samana; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of old age and death.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of grief and delusion; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of hunger and thirst.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of sound and the elements that arise; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of Hiranyagarbha.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of the dream state; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of Taijasa and the like.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of harm and the like; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of knowledge of the assembly.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of superimposition; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of sattva and the other qualities.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of being and non-being; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of all parts.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of difference and non-difference; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of the state of deep sleep.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of the condition of Prajna; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of "m" and the like.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of the measurer and the measured; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of measure and its source.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of witness-hood and the like; I am Brahman, the supreme light, free of cause and effect.
Brahman, the fourth state (turiya), is free of body, senses, mind, intellect, prana and ego, released from waking, dream, deep sleep and the rest.
Eternal, pure, awake, free, truth, bliss, without a second: I am Brahman, with knowledge, liberated, Om. I am Brahman, the supreme light; samadhi is the supreme giver of liberation.
Of complete lordship, valour, fame, prosperity, knowledge and dispassion — these six are called "bhaga".
Beings dwell in Vishnu, and he is the Sustainer of three natures. Thus the word "Bhagavan" is used elsewhere only figuratively; it truly belongs to Hari.
He who knows the origin and dissolution of beings, their coming and going, knowledge and ignorance, is to be called "Bhagavan".
Power of knowledge, supreme lordship, valour and splendour in full, without the faults to be avoided: these are meant by the word Bhagavan.
Keshidhvaja formerly taught yoga to Khandikya Janaka: the notion of self in what is not the self, and the notion "this is mine"...
...are the origin of ignorance; this seed is firmly twofold. In the body made of five elements, the embodied one, resting in the darkness of delusion,
loudly makes the judgment "I am this" — the dull-witted. Likewise toward sons and grandsons produced by that body,
the learned one treats the non-self body as equal; a man performs action for the benefit of all bodies.
When the body is different from the Person, then it leads only to bondage. This Self is of the nature of nirvana, of knowledge, stainless.
The misery, ignorance and unrighteousness belong to Prakriti, not to the Self. Water has contact with fire only through the pot.
The sounds "ka" and the like are properties made by that, O great sage. So the Self, through contact with Prakriti, is adorned with "I" and "mine".
It takes on Prakriti's properties, yet it is other than them, imperishable. For bondage there is attachment to objects; for knowledge, a mind without objects.
Drawing the mind away from objects, one should remember Hari, who is Brahman. He leads the one who meditates on Brahman to the state of the Self, O sage.
By one's own power, as a magnet draws iron: the mind's movement, dependent on one's effort, is distinguished.
Its union with Brahman is called yoga. Motionless and established in samadhi, one reaches the Supreme Brahman.
By yamas and niyamas, posture, withdrawal, conquest of the winds, by pranayama and control of breath, and by withdrawal of the senses...
...having subdued them, one should then fix the mind on an auspicious support. The support of the mind is Brahman, twofold: with form and without form.
Sanandana and others are joined with meditation on the nature of Brahman; others, gods and so on down to the immovable, with meditation on action.
In Hiranyagarbha and others it is twofold, of knowledge and of action; meditation is declared threefold; the universe is worshipped as Brahman.
That in which all difference has set, mere being, beyond the reach of speech, known to the Self — that knowledge is called Brahman.
That is Vishnu's supreme form, formless, unborn, imperishable; since it is hard to meditate on first, one should contemplate the form-bearing aspects.
Having attained the state of true being, he then becomes non-different from the Supreme Self; difference is created by ignorance.
